evidence:
Authority and scope: opened the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl, Quality Checks row 36 (number 35), plus Internal Quality Checks row 36. The shipped row requires a criterion proving defining behavior and, where required, reload/re-auth survival and server-backed state. Frozen rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:145-147 says the same and distinguishes server-backed from same-origin. Applied qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md sections Independent credit, Gates must exclude convincing dead apps, and Runtime and model evidence. No sign-in is appropriate: task/instruction.md:1 and tests/app_context.md, Accounts, explicitly describe a public shared library. Paths beginning task/ or rules/ below are under .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/.

Defining behavior is directly graded. task/instruction.md:1-3 asks to author JS/HTML/CSS, see results, save useful snippets and restore the last working preview after errors/Stop. tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 requires an original distinctive document.body.textContent marker and console.log marker, actual editor source, pressing Run, and observing both outputs; it explicitly rejects an editor-only marker, hardcoded sample or dead Run. Functional judge.toml:46,53,179 separately owns filename-based JS/HTML execution, CSS application and latest-good-preview rollback. The prompt requires observed browser outcomes, not source-reading as a substitute (tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:7,13,17).

Durability is an explicit public promise and explicit grading target. environment/instructions/integration.md:7 says saved snippets, identities and revisions survive browser reload and complete process restart over the same database. behaviour.md:25 requires exact title/filename/source and distinct new records. tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29 requires a successful normal UI write and its observed server response, retrieval of that newly authored identity and exact fields in an independent clean browser context without copied storage, and another reload/readback. It rejects a health response, toast, static seed or localStorage alone. It expressly accepts server-rendered documents and does not require a JSON endpoint or same-origin assertion. constraints/prompt.md:24-33 supplies the newContext lifecycle. Thus a frontend-only localStorage library cannot satisfy the specified evidence even though it survives an ordinary reload.

Independent scored durability outcomes are present at tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:333-358. S21's protocol (prompt.md:354-357) saves Alpha and Beta as separate records, loads each exact field, reloads, then loads both again. S22 (prompt.md:363-369) creates two ordinary records, updates one, records identities/revisions, invokes restart_app exactly once, reads both and the recorded library after completion, and separately tests a subsequent valid save. Its fallback preserves continued-write credit when old-record survival fails; a later write failure does not erase valid durability credit. The criteria do not demand persisted console history, live preview, theme, or authentication across reload where the public task does not promise them.

Raw evidence independently inspected: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json, facts S21.saved_records_browser_reload at line 8572, S22.process_restart_durability at 8601, and S22.process_restart_write at 8759. Alpha id 1 and Beta id 2 retain their different exact sources after reload. Primary id 3 has source console.log('restart-before-restart'); and revision 2, while Second id 4 has console.log('restart-second'); and revision 1. actual-restart.json records exactly one canonical restart call, PID 16 to 335, and a successful MCP response. Before/after arrays contain identical complete records for ids 1-4 exactly once; I independently compared those arrays and uniqueness rather than relying on product_pass. The later readback contains only Primary's intended change to console.log('restart-after-save'); and revision 3, with every other complete record unchanged. The recorded S21/S22 browser actions all completed.

The executed drivers substantiate those observations: drivers/library_flow.cjs:25-47 performs UI saves, actual reload, field-checked loads, complete-array comparisons, restart assertions, and post-restart write/readback. drivers/workflow_core.cjs:142-175 observes real successful mutation responses, asserts loaded title/filename/source/revision, fetches the previously observed library URL, and calls page.reload(). drivers/run_workflow.cjs:20-24 creates a fresh Chromium context for each pre/post phase; lines 48-50 execute S21/S22 around the restart. The saved app-restart.sh uses the same /tmp/cw-structural-workflow/app/app.db path. Source corroboration, separate from runtime proof: solution/app/server.js:8,66-88,113-128 opens the durable DB_PATH SQLite file and reads/writes stored records; solution/app/src/app.tsx:47-69 refreshes and saves through that server. Read-only SHA256 verification found zero mismatches across all 22 actual_app_files and all 17 recorded driver files; frozen functional criteria, functional prompt and restart_mcp.py hashes also match.

The raw defining-behavior observations also show js-dispatch-ok plus js-dispatch-log, HTML output, and CSS computed color rgb(255, 0, 0) while retaining the prior authored background (RESULTS.json facts S02.js_html_filename_dispatch and S02.css_apply_snapshot). S10.js_error_rollback records distinct prior timeout-recovered and latest-good-B renders, followed by restored latest-good-B. These are scripted product observations, not a full configured judge run. The raw record explicitly says direct pinned Playwright, paid_provider false, and oracle_score_claimed false. No Oracle reward, target-model score, configured-judge completion, or judge workload clearance is inferred for this row.

Counterexample review: a convincing playground shell whose Run only echoes editor text and whose library lives in localStorage is rejected by the authored-output gate and clean-context server-data requirement; an in-memory server library that loses data on restart is rejected by S22. These are source-level rejection witnesses, not newly executed weak-app tests. A conforming implementation using server-rendered library documents, different routes/field names/UI labels, and public CDN assets remains acceptable under constraints/judge.toml:25-29 and functional/prompt.md:5,11,13,19. No plausible unresolved false-pass or false-fail witness was found for the specific core-behavior/durability check.
